ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is brown with a dark, broad lateral stripe and a distinct white upper lip. Key features include long, slender limbs and a smooth, glandular back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Clinotarsus alticola* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark brown to blackish lateral head stripe that covers the entire tympanum, contrasting sharply with its pale belly.
ai.habitat: The Assam Hills Frog inhabits primary evergreen and semi-evergreen tropical forests, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Assam Hills Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky banks of mountain streams under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Clinotarsus alticola* is an oviparous breeder that deposits large clutches of eggs in stagnant forest pools. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assam Hills Frog is found in Northeast India, specifically across Assam, Meghalaya, and Arunachal Pradesh, typically inhabiting hilly regions at moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Assam Hills Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in hilly forest habitats.
